assumptions: 0<gamma<1.
The null is independence and each alternative has fixed positive covariance.
The rule is interpreted in exact real arithmetic.
inherited_statement.conclusion: The probability of ever falsely selecting the dependent alternative under the null is at most gamma, while every fixed positive alternative is detected in finite time almost surely.
inherited_statement.input_contract: iid binary pairs; empirical c_n=b_n-p_n q_n; epsilon_n=sqrt(log(6n(n+1)/gamma)/(2n)); stop only for c_n>3 epsilon_n.
limitations: The rule returns no null answer and has no uniform finite stopping-time guarantee.
No verified floating-point classifier is supplied.
Conservative numerical errors and thresholds must still vanish for the eventual-detection argument.

inherited_result_bindings.title: No uniformly reliable terminating null branch without separation

assumptions: The procedure is nonanticipating.
It terminates almost surely under the fixed null.
Uniform null and alternative error bounds sum to less than one.
inherited_statement.conclusion: No such two-answer procedure exists over the full near-null alternative class: finite stopping prefixes can be approximated by alternatives closely enough to retain the null decision probability.
inherited_statement.input_contract: Fixed uniform independent-pair null at x=0,v=1,k=3,r_a=0 and alternatives delta=(1-2 epsilon)/6 decreasing to zero.
limitations: The theorem does not require alternative-side almost-sure termination or finite expected stopping time.
Separated subclasses can admit stronger services.
It is an exact model result, not a general impossibility of all empirical science.
